statement: A large robot mower can cut a field on its own in 3 hours. A small robot mower can cut the same field on its own in 6 hours. The small mower starts alone. After 2 hours the large mower joins it, and they finish the field together. How long does the whole job take, counted from the start?

choices.misconception: I worked out how long the two mowers take together from the very start, and left out the 2 hours the small mower worked alone.
I thought two mowers finish the rest in half the time the small one would need alone, so 4 hours became 2 more hours.
I thought the whole job takes the average of 3 hours and 6 hours.
I added the small mower's 2 hours to the 3 hours the large mower takes on its own.

hints: Think about what fraction of the field each mower cuts in one hour.
Work in fractions of the field. Find how much the small mower has cut before help arrives, then how fast the two mowers cut together, and divide the part that is left by that combined speed.
In 2 hours the small mower cuts 2/6 = 1/3 of the field, so 2/3 is left. Together they cut 1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2 of the field per hour, so 2/3 takes (2/3) ÷ (1/2) = 4/3 hours.

solutions.reliable: Per hour, the large mower cuts 1/3 of the field and the small one cuts 1/6. In the first 2 hours the small mower alone cuts 2 × 1/6 = 1/3, leaving 2/3. Working together they cut 1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2 of the field per hour, so the remaining 2/3 takes (2/3) ÷ (1/2) = 4/3 hours, which is 1 hour 20 minutes. The whole job takes 2 hours + 1 hour 20 minutes = 3 hours 20 minutes. The transferable idea: in work problems, add speeds (fractions of the job per hour), never times.
solutions.elegant: Count in small-mower hours: the large mower does as much in one hour as the small mower does in two. The field is 6 small-mower hours of work. After 2 hours, 4 small-mower hours remain, and together they do 3 small-mower hours each hour, so they need 4/3 hours more. Total 3 hours 20 minutes.

whyOnTest: Combined work at 4 points adds a twist: one worker starts alone, so you must split the job before adding rates.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
